issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) define and use a class named Meal (constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters) as the domain entity for menu items, but the template repository does not provide a Meal implementation: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java is empty and the template instead contains a class named Order with the same fields/constructor shape. Main in the template also uses Order in its examples. This inconsistent identifier usage (Meal vs Order) across problem statement, template, and solution will confuse students, cause mismatches between instructions and starter code, and may lead to compilation issues or duplicated/incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the conceptual entity name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) Replace the template's Order class with a Meal class (rename file/class or copy implementation) that matches the problem statement and solution (constructor Meal(String, String[]) plus getters), update Main to use Meal, and remove the extraneous Order class; OR (B) if Order is intentional, update the problem statement, UML, examples, and solution to use Order everywhere. Ensure example code, tests, and starter files reference the same class name so students can follow instructions without renaming or duplicating classes.
